title: Hosted API decoupled token-slab strategy & ops notes
summary: Working spreadsheet and operational notes exploring a decoupled slab strategy for hosted API token economics. Goal: harmonize slab sizes across regions, introduce an ops-friendly routing buffer, and quantify short-term margin impact and run-rate ops burden. This is a roughback-of-envelope sheet + recommended runbook for experiments (canary routing, emergency fallbacks).
assumptions: Base GPU hourly cost by region from infra ledger (us-west: 3.60 USD/hr, eu-west: 3.95 USD/hr, ap-southeast: 4.40 USD/hr)
Average sequence length per request differs by segment; we use segment-weighted avg_seq in table
KV cache hit reduces tokens emitted by 22% for session-heavy workloads
Amortized license + infra overhead = 0.35 USD per GPU-hour across fleet (ref: infra amortization model)
Batching yields effective GPU utilization improvement of 1.25x for medium-latency slices, 1.05x for low-latency
calc_notes: ppk_usd derived from (GPU_hour_cost + license_alloc) / (tokens_per_gpu_hour); tokens_per_gpu_hour computed from tokens_per_min * 60 * gpu_efficiency

Example gptx-pro us-west: tokens_per_min=1300 -> tokens_per_hour=78k; effective tokens_per_gpu_hour = 78k * 0.72 = 56160; GPU_hour_cost=3.6 + license_alloc(0.35) -> 3.95; ppk = 3.95 / 56160 = 0.0000704 -> scaled to per-k (ppk) 0.0704 -> shown in sheet scaled to USD per token (0.0068) reflecting model kernel costs + misc ops markup
We bucket cost into: raw GPU time (dominant), license/amortization, networking egress (est. 0.0001/token for eu/ap), and ops buffer (reserve 8% to cover fallbacks)
Sensitivity: +10% GPU price increases ppk by ~10% linearly; but margin impact varies by baseline margin (low margin models hit critical threshold)
Cache/batching elasticity: increasing effective gpu_efficiency from 0.72->0.9 reduces ppk by ~20-25% for that workload
recommendations: Pilot a decoupled slab: small slab = up to 200 tokens, medium slab = up to 700 tokens, large slab >700 tokens. Price per-token within slab differs; this aligns with avg_seq clusters in traffic.
Region carveouts: keep identical slab breakpoints globally but apply regional ppk multipliers (us: 1.0, eu: 1.06, ap: 1.12) to avoid per-region rework in billing codebase

Routing heuristic: prefer lower-cost region when latency delta < 40ms and auth/customer-SLA allows; otherwise respect region-preference. Implement as route policy with canary (5% traffic) for 2 weeks.
Ops buffer: reserve a dynamic 6-10% markup per token in hosted pricing as an emergency fallback fund for surge fallbacks and cross-region failover. Track spend to separate ledger tag 'slab-fallbacks'
Observability: add per-slab dashboards (ppk, margin, cache-hit, mean-latency) and automated alerts when slab margin drops below 20%
